name: Rootkit & Kernel Analysis
description: Ability to detect and analyse kernel-level rootkits and manipulation through memory forensics. Covers DKOM (Direct Kernel Object Manipulation), kernel callback enumeration, driver analysis including bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver abuse, ETW tampering, bootkit indicators in memory, and the legacy SSDT and IDT hooking techniques still seen on x86. Requires deep understanding of OS kernel internals.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to rootkit or kernel-level memory analysis

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands the concept of kernel-level rootkits and why they are difficult to detect from a running system
evidence: Can explain what a rootkit is and how kernel-mode rootkits differ from user-mode
Understands DKOM, SSDT hooking, and driver-based rootkit concepts at a high level
Can describe why memory forensics is essential for rootkit detection

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Uses Volatility kernel analysis plugins to scan for rootkit indicators under supervision
evidence: Ran Volatility ssdt, callbacks, driverscan, and modules plugins under guidance
Compared loaded driver lists with on-disk driver files to identify discrepancies
Identified DKOM-hidden processes using cross-referencing techniques (pslist vs. psscan)
Documented kernel analysis findings with supervisor review

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently detects kernel-level compromise and rootkits in memory dumps and reports findings with technical accuracy
evidence: Independently identified kernel rootkits or DKOM manipulation in 3+ investigations
Correctly determined rootkit persistence mechanisms from memory evidence
Extracted and analysed malicious kernel drivers from memory dumps
Produced rootkit analysis reports with clear technical explanations for case findings

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Analyses advanced kernel exploitation and bootkits; develops detection capabilities for new rootkit techniques
evidence: Detected bootkit indicators in memory and corroborated suspected firmware-level persistence with firmware or disk acquisition
Analysed rootkits using advanced kernel patching or hypervisor-based subversion
Developed custom detection plugins for emerging kernel-level threats
Mentors analysts on kernel internals and rootkit detection methodology

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines kernel forensics methodology; researches new kernel attack surfaces; recognised authority in rootkit detection
evidence: Authored or maintains the lab's kernel forensics and rootkit detection procedures
Published research on kernel rootkit techniques or detection methods
Contributes to open-source kernel forensics tooling or frameworks
Trains teams and presents on advanced kernel forensics at conferences or in training courses

assessment_methods.description: Analyse a memory dump from a system compromised with a kernel rootkit, identify the rootkit technique, extract artifacts, and document findings
Given a memory dump with subtle kernel manipulation, determine whether rootkit activity is present and characterise the technique used
